content:
maria: quick question — we need a final decision on how to split traffic by plan when a region is overloaded. free/pro/enterprise expectations?
aj: high level: free should fall back aggressively to cheaper variants, pro should try warm variants then degrade, enterprise gets multiregional failover and quota priority.
sophie: agree. Also need to surface this in the console UX so customers see 'degrade mode' + reason. otherwise support gets flooded.
priya: telemetry ask: track reason code (quota|region|latency) + final model id for each request. that lets Optimize recommend changes.
tom: small nit — do we do soft quota for free (i.e., return 429-like header but still serve cheaper model) or hard block?
aj: i'm leaning soft for free: give best-effort with a warning header and metric. hard block for pro only if abuse. enterprise always respect committed capacity.
maria: +1 on soft for free. but need guardrails to avoid crazy token cost if cheap variant still expensive. maybe cap tokens for fallback streams.
sophie: UX: show a per-plan 'routing policy' card with toggles: prefer-regional, allow-variant-fallback, soft-quota. default for free: allow-variant-fallback=true, soft-quota=true.
priya: quick config sketch (for discussion):
```json
{
  "routing_policies": {
    "free": {
      "priority_order": ["local_v1_quant", "regional_v1", "cross_region_v1"],
      "quota_enforcement": "soft",
      "max_tokens_on_fallback": 512
    },
    "pro": {
      "priority_order": ["local_v2", "regional_v2", "local_v1_quant"],
      "quota_enforcement": "hard",
      "grace_burst": 200
    },
    "enterprise": {
      "priority_order": ["local_v2", "regional_v2", "cross_region_v2"],
      "quota_enforcement": "hard",
      "multiregional_failover": true
    }
  }
}
```
aj: love the schema. Note: we must clearly separate policy (what to try) from enforcement (what to count/charge). logs should include attempted_variants list.
tom: ops question — what does the runtime do when quota_enforcement=soft and fallback model is much slower? do we return immediately with a warning or queue briefly?
priya: runtime idea: fast-path try best local model with a 150ms latency SLO, if exceeds, fall back to next variant. For soft-quota, allow fallback but attach header x-redwood-degraded: true and metric redwood.degraded_variant=true.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-policy-service v3 -> canary on prod at 23:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: canary started on host group rg-routing-02 (ID: rg-02). monitoring hooks ready.
maria: can we add a telemetry field 'policy_decision' with enum {OK_PRIMARY, FALLBACK_VARIANT, REGIONAL_REDIRECT, RATE_LIMITED}? that will help dashboards.
sophie: +1 — saves support time. Will add column to per-tenant trace view.
aj: enforcement semantics proposal:
- soft: still accept, mark and charge at fallback rate.
- hard: reject with 429 and reason header.
- committed: enterprise reserved pools, no fallback without explicit override.
priya: need a hidden opt-in flag 'prefer_cost_savings' for tenants who want maximum savings (even if quality loss). expose as plan-level toggle.
maria: edge-case: what if fallback variant changes internal API (different function-calling behavior)? must validate compatibility before routing. add a compatibility check step in policy engine.
tom: compatibility matrix is a pain but doable. store minimal capability flags per model (functions:true/false, tool-signatures:v1) and match at decision time.
sophie: for the console rollout UX: initial beta expose 'routing policy preview' to a subset of orgs and show estimated cost delta + latency delta.
aj: prod telemetry items to add: policy_decision, attempted_variants, final_model_id, latency_ms, token_counts, quota_remaining_at_decision.
priya: agree — plus anomaly alert when fallback rate > 5% for an org over 1h.
maria: who owns the policy editor front-end? @sophie?
sophie: i'll take the UI card + preview. @aj can you wire up the policy API and make it return the decision hints?
aj: yep will add /v1/policies/:tenant preview endpoint. will include simulation flag.
maria: timeline? this week for API proto, next week for console beta. sound good?
sophie: sounds good. will sketch mocks today. :white_check_mark:
priya: i'll add telemetry schema PR.
tom: i'll schedule a runbook for 'fallback surge' incident playbook.
maria: thanks team — i'll post an RFC with config docs and example console flows.
aj: one more: do we emit cost_estimate for each decision? would be really helpful for Optimize integration.
priya: adding cost_estimate to telemetry.
maria: ok closing thread — will follow up on RFC. :wave:
